frictionSummary: Self-serve, instant, no review — but tokens expire after 8h by default now.
prerequisites: Admin access to the org, if the app will belong to one
A homepage URL and at least one redirect URI, even a placeholder for local dev

steps.title: Open Developer settings
steps.body: GitHub Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps → New OAuth App (github.com/settings/applications/new).

steps.title: Fill in app details and redirect URIs
steps.body: Application name, homepage URL, and a redirect URI. GitHub now supports up to 10 redirect URIs per app (added/removed individually), each with an optional wildcard-matching toggle — it's no longer a single callback field.

steps.title: Decide on token expiration before you register
steps.body: "Expire user access tokens" is checked by default on new apps: access tokens last 8 hours and come with a refresh token. If your integration only does the one-time code-for-token exchange, it will silently stop working after 8 hours unless you handle refresh tokens or opt out under Optional features.

steps.title: Register and generate a client secret
steps.body: GitHub shows the client secret exactly once. Exchange the authorization code for a token like this:
steps.codeSnippet:
curl -X POST https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -d client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID \
  -d client_secret=YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET \
  -d code=THE_AUTH_CODE

steps.title: Store credentials and go live
steps.body: Save the client ID and secret as environment variables. No submission or review step — the app works immediately, though new/small apps show trust warnings to users on the authorize screen.

scopes.grants: Full access to public and private repositories

approval.notes: GitHub does not gate OAuth Apps behind manual review. Only certain GitHub Apps Marketplace listings require that. Verified hands-on: registered a real OAuth app and reached the authorize screen with no review step anywhere in the flow.

gotchas: Redirect URIs are now a list (up to 10), not a single field — older tutorials assume one callback URL
"Expire user access tokens" defaults to ON for new apps: 8-hour access tokens + refresh token, not the old non-expiring token
The client secret is shown once; losing it means generating a new one
New/small apps show trust warnings on the authorize screen ("Not owned or operated by GitHub", "Created less than a day ago", "Fewer than 10 GitHub users") — expect early users to see this
Organization-owned apps need an org admin to approve third-party access if the org restricts it

do: Install @octokit/oauth-app (or use plain fetch) for the token exchange
Create /api/auth/github/callback — exchanges the auth code for a token at https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token
Add placeholder env vars: GITHUB_CLIENT_ID, GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET, GITHUB_REDIRECT_URI
Wire up a "Connect GitHub" button that redirects to https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize?scope=read:user,user:email
Handle token refresh: if token expiration is left on, store the refresh_token and re-exchange it before the 8h access token expires
dont: Register the OAuth app at github.com/settings/developers — that's the developer's call
Enter the real client secret anywhere — leave it as an env placeholder
Assume the access token never expires — check whether the app owner left token expiration on
